# Factory events reference

Generated from [`schemas/`](schemas/); the decisions are in [`README.md`](README.md).

## Types

| Type | Versions | Issue | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`abandoned`](#abandoned) | v1 | required | The factory stopped work on the issue and it left the factory without a merge: its factory labels are off and no device will take it until someone labels it ready again. |
| [`claim_lost`](#claim_lost) | v1 | required | This device tried to claim the issue and another device holds it. |
| [`claim_renewed`](#claim_renewed) | v1 | required | A heartbeat extended this device's claim on the issue. |
| [`claimed`](#claimed) | v1 | required | This device took the claim on the issue: no other device works on it while the lease holds. |
| [`closed`](#closed) | v1 | required | GitHub shows the issue closed, outside the factory's own merge. |
| [`finding_handled`](#finding_handled) | v1 | required | The fixer fixed or declined one review finding. |
| [`gate_run`](#gate_run) | v1 | required | One run of the stop gate in a writer's slot finished: the repo's gate commands ran, or the gate never got a turn. |
| [`implementer_routed`](#implementer_routed) | v1 | required | The model for the issue's build step was chosen. |
| [`intervention`](#intervention) | v1 | optional | Someone had to step in where the plan did not foresee it: a person (an owner op, a push, a hand merge, a rescue), the loop's judge (the main conversation, running a control op through the control tool) or the loop with unplanned judgement or recovery (a triage, an unknown step, a park, a guard refusal). |
| [`loop_entry`](#loop_entry) | v1 | optional | Loop bookkeeping that most consumers can ignore: one piece of the loop's own work (an agent step, a tell to the owner, or a task) changed status. |
| [`loop_passes`](#loop_passes) | v1 | none | Loop bookkeeping that most consumers can ignore: a summary of one UTC minute of the loop's passes (how many ended, how long they took, how many acted or threw), written once a minute while the loop runs. |
| [`merged`](#merged) | v1 | optional | A pull request for the issue was merged. |
| [`ready`](#ready) | v1 | required | The issue was seen with the ready label: it is in the factory's queue. |
| [`requeued`](#requeued) | v1 | required | The issue's claim was given back and the issue is in the queue again (ready label on), for any device to take. |
| [`reviewed`](#reviewed) | v1 | required | One review of the issue's pull request finished. |
| [`shadow_read`](#shadow_read) | v1 | none | One shadow compare made by a reader that has an old/new source switch: the command read the same keys from the old source and the new central one and counted where the answers differ. |
| [`test_weakened`](#test_weakened) | v1 | required | A commit on a merged pull request deleted or weakened a test (removed an assertion, added a skip, .only, --warn-only or \|\| true, or commented an assertion out). |
| [`transition`](#transition) | v1 | required | The loop's record of the issue changed: it moved to a new state, or its step, attempt or notes changed. |
| [`untrusted_stripped`](#untrusted_stripped) | v1 | required | A read of GitHub content dropped text by untrusted authors, or refused an untrusted issue, pull request or comment outright. |
| [`usage`](#usage) | v1 | none | A reading of the Claude subscription's usage windows. |
| [`wind_down`](#wind_down) | v1 | none | One stop of a workspace's loop finished winding down: the loop stopped taking new work, waited for the steps that were running (up to a cap), then stopped. |

## Envelope

One factory event: the fields every event has, with its payload in data. One line in the local event log, one row in the factory database.

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `envelope` | const 1 | required | no |  |  | The version of this envelope. A reader refuses one it does not know. |
| `event_id` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |  | A UUID the writer makes. The event's identity: a re-push or a retried insert never makes a second row. |
| `ts` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` |  | When the event was written: UTC, ISO 8601, always with exactly three millisecond digits (2026-10-16T15:45:19.123Z), so times sort and compare as text. |
| `type` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z_]*$` |  | The event type, for example claimed or transition. Names the payload's schema with type_version. |
| `type_version` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 |  | The version of this type's payload. data is valid against schemas/<type>.v<type_version>.json. |
| `repo` | string | required | no | pattern `^[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+$` |  | The repository whose factory wrote it, as owner/name. |
| `device` | string | required | no | minLength 1 |  | The machine that wrote it: DEV_MACHINE_NAME, else the hostname. |
| `actor` | string | required | no | minLength 1 |  | The tool or role that wrote it, for example sweep, watcher, fixer or factory-reconcile; agent when the caller named none. For provenance only: what a reader needs to know is in the type and the payload. |
| `session_id` | string | required | yes |  |  | The Claude session that wrote it, from CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, else CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (Claude Code sets it); null when both are unset. Never guessed. |
| `issue` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 |  | The GitHub issue the event is about; null for a fleet-level event. Each type's schema says whether it is required (x-issue). |
| `base_image` | string | required | yes |  |  | The base image version running when it was written; null when unknown. |
| `dev_image` | string | required | yes |  |  | The repo's dev image version running when it was written; null when unknown or none. |
| `template_version` | string | required | yes |  |  | The Coder template version running when it was written; null when unknown. |
| `plugin_version` | string | required | yes |  |  | The callum-flow plugin version running when it was written; null when unknown. |
| `data` | object | required | no |  |  | The payload: a flat object whose fields the type's schema describes. |

Example:

```json
{
  "envelope": 1,
  "event_id": "3f1c9a52-8b0e-4f7a-9d21-6c4e2b7a1f08",
  "ts": "2026-10-16T15:45:19.123Z",
  "type": "claimed",
  "type_version": 1,
  "repo": "cbundy/plant-console",
  "device": "coder-plant-console-loop",
  "actor": "agent",
  "session_id": null,
  "issue": 92,
  "base_image": "2.31.0",
  "dev_image": null,
  "template_version": "dev-system-v41",
  "plugin_version": "0.40.0",
  "data": {
    "lease_minutes": 120
  }
}
```

| `session_id` | string | every event | The Claude session that wrote it, from CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, else CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (Claude Code sets it); null when both are unset. Never guessed. |
| `issue` | integer | every event | The GitHub issue the event is about; null for a fleet-level event. Each type's schema says whether it is required (x-issue). |

| `dev_image` | string | every event | The repo's dev image version running when it was written; null when unknown or none. |

| `plugin_version` | string | every event | The callum-flow plugin version running when it was written; null when unknown. |

| `acting` | integer | `loop_passes` | Of those passes, how many acted (did something rather than finding nothing to do). |
| `acting_mean_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The mean duration of the acting passes, in milliseconds, rounded; null when none acted. |
| `additions` | integer | `merged` | The pull request's total lines added, as GitHub reports them at merge time. null when unknown. |

| `answer_path` | string | `reviewed` | The reviewer's answer file on the loop's device. Identifies the review: one event per answer. |
| `attempt` | integer | `transition` | The attempt of that step, from 1. |
| `attempts` | integer | `loop_entry` | Attempts of this key so far. |
| `available` | boolean | `usage` | true when a reading was had; false when no source gave one (then every reading field is null). |
| `branch` | string | `abandoned`, `finding_handled`, `merged`, `requeued`, `reviewed`, `test_weakened`, `transition` | The abandoned work's branch, when known. |
| `brief_url` | string | `transition` | The URL of the design brief comment; null until the designer posts one. |
| `bucket` | integer | `implementer_routed` | hash: the issue's stable bucket, 0 to 99 (Opus when below opus_pct); null otherwise. |
| `by` | enum | `merged` | factory: the factory merged it; hand: a person merged it outside the factory. |
| `cap_ms` | integer | `wind_down` | The longest the stop was allowed to wait, in milliseconds. |
| `cause` | string | `intervention` | What happened, as a code of v2 SPEC 7.2: for example op:resume, push, hand-merge, rescue, restart, config-file, triage, park, unknown:timeout, free:load, fix:ci or guard:write. An open list: handle a code you do not know. |
| `class` | enum | `loop_entry` | The planner's class for the work. |
| `compared` | integer | `shadow_read` | How many keys were compared. |
| `concurrency` | integer | `gate_run` | How many gates could run at once when this one asked for a turn; null when there was no limit. |
| `cut_at_stop` | integer | `wind_down` | How many steps were still running, and cut, when the loop stopped. |
| `cut_at_stop_keys` | array of string | `wind_down` | The loop keys of the cut steps, in the same form as running_at_request_keys. Lifted as a jsonb column so a cut step can be joined to its re-run. |
| `deletions` | integer | `merged` | The pull request's total lines deleted, as GitHub reports them at merge time. null when unknown. |
| `differences` | integer | `shadow_read` | How many keys whose answers differ, with both sides cut at the settle time. |
| `ended_at` | string | `loop_entry` | When it ended; null while running. |
| `errors` | integer | `loop_passes`, `reviewed` | Of those passes, how many threw. |
| `fact` | string | `intervention` | The key of the fact it records, so it is logged and counted once; null for a hand-recorded rescue. |
| `files` | array of string | `merged`, `test_weakened` | The repo-relative paths the merged pull request changed, taken from GitHub's pull request files at merge time. Complete up to GitHub's own cap on that list. null when unknown, for example on a recovered merge or a pr of null. |
| `five_hour_pct` | integer | `usage` | Percent of the five-hour window used, rounded up. |
| `five_hour_resets_at` | string | `usage` | When the five-hour window resets. |
| `fixes` | integer | `transition` | Loop state, for the record rebuild: entries to fixing so far in this life. |
| `from_at` | string | `loop_passes` | The start of the UTC minute summed up, inclusive. |
| `from_state` | enum | `transition` | The state before; null for a life's first transition. |
| `head` | string | `finding_handled`, `gate_run`, `merged`, `reviewed`, `test_weakened`, `transition` | The head after the fix step, when known. |
| `idle_mean_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The mean duration of the passes that did not act, in milliseconds, rounded; null when every pass acted or there was none. |
| `key` | string | `loop_entry` | The ledger key: the work's identity across retries, for example i92/ltn0brb/review/0821e6a/r2/a1. |
| `kind` | enum | `loop_entry` | agent-step: an agent ran one step of an issue; tell: a message to the owner; task: a wake of the loop's model outside a planned step. |
| `labels` | array of string | `claimed`, `ready` | The issue's label names in GitHub's order, as the producer read them: on ready, the labels of the queue listing; on claimed, the labels after the claim (the ready label the claim removed is left out). Null when they were not read. |
| `lease_minutes` | integer | `claim_renewed`, `claimed` | How long the claim now holds from this event, in minutes. |
| `life` | string | `gate_run`, `intervention`, `transition` | Which life of the issue the gate ran in. |
| `live_differences` | integer | `shadow_read` | How many keys whose answers differ on everything read, push lag included. |
| `lives` | integer | `abandoned`, `requeued`, `transition` | reconcile and rejected: the released life's number among the issue's lives, when known; null otherwise. |
| `max_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The longest duration, in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `mean_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The mean duration of the passes, in milliseconds, rounded; null when there was none. |
| `mode` | enum | `loop_passes` | The loop's mode: off, observe (plans, does not act) or act. |
| `model` | string | `implementer_routed` | The model alias chosen, for example sonnet or opus. |
| `new_ok` | boolean | `shadow_read` | Whether the central read of the new side succeeded. |
| `notes` | array of string | `transition` | Loop state, for the record rebuild: owner, triage and decline notes for this seq's step, oldest first. For people and the step's agent; never parse them. |
| `old_ok` | boolean | `shadow_read` | Whether the central read of the old side succeeded. |
| `opus_pct` | integer | `implementer_routed` | The configured share of issues routed to Opus, in percent. |
| `outcome` | enum | `finding_handled`, `wind_down` | fixed: the fixer changed the code for it; declined: the fixer judged it wrong or not worth a change. |
| `p50_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The median duration (nearest rank), in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `p90_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The 90th percentile duration (nearest rank), in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `parent` | integer | `claimed`, `ready` | The parent issue's number when the parent is in the same repo. Null when there is no parent, when the parent is in another repo, or when it was not read. |
| `pass_every_ms` | integer | `loop_passes` | The loop's configured time between passes, in milliseconds. |
| `passes` | integer | `loop_passes` | Passes that ended in the minute. 0 when none did; then every duration below is null. |
| `patch` | string | `reviewed` | The patch id reviewed: an approval holds for exactly this patch. |
| `planner` | enum | `loop_passes` | Which planner the loop ran. |
| `pr` | integer | `abandoned`, `finding_handled`, `intervention`, `merged`, `requeued`, `reviewed`, `test_weakened`, `transition`, `untrusted_stripped` | The abandoned work's pull request, when there is one. |
| `question` | string | `transition` | parked: the question for the owner; null otherwise. For people; never parse it. |
| `queued_behind` | integer | `gate_run` | How many gates held a turn or waited ahead of this one when it asked; 0 when it took a turn at once. |
| `reader` | string | `shadow_read` | Which reader was compared, an open family such as claim-events. |
| `reason` | enum or string | `abandoned`, `closed`, `implementer_routed`, `requeued` | Why: dropped (by the owner), split (the designer split it into new issues), triage (the triage agent dropped it), reconcile (reconcile found no live work behind the claim and took the issue out of the factory), rejected (released at its last allowed life and labelled factory:rejected), other. |
| `requested_at` | string | `wind_down` | When the stop was asked for. With outcome off it equals stopped_at. |
| `restored` | boolean | `test_weakened` | true when a later commit on the branch put the test back. |
| `result` | enum | `gate_run` | pass, fail (a command exited non-zero), or unknown (the gate could not run: its budget ran out, a command did not start, or it never got a turn within the wait cap). |
| `resume_to` | enum | `transition` | Loop state, for the record rebuild: when to_state is queued, the state a new claim leads to; when parked, the state unparking leads to; when waiting, the state the loop resumes to once every condition in wait holds; null otherwise. |
| `round` | integer | `reviewed`, `transition` | The review round in this life, from 1. |
| `run_ms` | integer | `gate_run` | How long the gate ran once it held a turn, in milliseconds; 0 when it never ran. |
| `running_at_request` | integer | `wind_down` | How many steps were running when the stop was asked for. |
| `seq` | integer | `gate_run`, `transition` | The record's sequence in this life whose writer step ran the gate. |
| `seq_at` | string | `transition` | When this transition happened. Time transitions by this, not by the envelope ts: a transition logged again after a re-claim keeps its seq_at. |
| `settle_seconds` | integer | `shadow_read` | The settle time in seconds: both sides are cut this far back so push lag is not counted as a difference. |
| `seven_day_pct` | integer | `usage` | Percent of the most used seven-day window, rounded up. |
| `seven_day_resets_at` | string | `usage` | When that seven-day window resets. |
| `split_into` | array of integer | `abandoned` | split: the new issues it was split into; empty otherwise. |
| `started_at` | string | `gate_run`, `loop_entry` | When the gate asked for its turn (before any wait). |
| `state_since` | string | `transition` | When the issue entered to_state; earlier than seq_at when the state did not change. |
| `status` | enum | `loop_entry` | The status it changed to. |
| `step` | enum | `transition` | The step this seq runs: the state's own step, or triage; null while waiting. |
| `stopped_at` | string | `wind_down` | When the loop stopped. With outcome off it equals requested_at. |
| `table_row` | string | `transition` | The row of the loop's transition table that fired, for example T9 or U1 (v2 SPEC 4.3); recovered when the loop rebuilt the record after losing the step's outcome, and then via is recovered too. |
| `title` | string | `claimed`, `ready` | The issue's title as the producer read it, clipped to 256 characters; null when it was not read. An issue's newest title is the title of its newest ready or claimed event by ts that has a non-null title. |
| `to_at` | string | `loop_passes` | The end of that minute, exclusive: one minute after from_at. |
| `to_state` | enum | `transition` | The state after: the issue's state from now on. |
| `tool` | string | `shadow_read` | The command that made the compare, such as callum-flow-sweep. |
| `triages` | integer | `transition` | Loop state, for the record rebuild: triage calls so far in this life. |
| `trigger` | string | `wind_down` | What asked for the stop: restart-self, coder-stop, or null when not known. |
| `verdict` | enum | `reviewed` | approve, changes (findings to fix), or unknown (no valid answer). |
| `via` | string | `transition` | A short code for what moved it, for example approve, fix:review, free:load, unknown:timeout, triage:retry, unreject, reclaim (logged again after a re-claim) or dual-write (logged again when the new log lacked it). An open list: handle a code you do not know. |
| `wait_ms` | integer | `gate_run` | How long the gate waited for a turn, in milliseconds; 0 when it took a turn at once or there is no limit. |
| `waited_ms` | integer | `wind_down` | How long the stop waited for running steps, in milliseconds; 0 with outcome off. |
| `who` | enum | `intervention` | person: a person did something; loop: the loop had to judge or recover; judge: the loop's judge (the main conversation) ran a control op through the control tool. |
| `why` | enum | `transition` | closed: why the life ended; null otherwise. |

## abandoned

The factory stopped work on the issue and it left the factory without a merge: its factory labels are off and no device will take it until someone labels it ready again. Written by the loop (an owner drop, a designer's split, a triage drop, a reconcile release) and by factory-reconcile. Ends the claim. The GitHub issue is not closed by this. A reconcile release that puts the issue back in the queue is requeued instead.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### abandoned v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | enum | required | no | one of "dropped", "split", "triage", "reconcile", "rejected", "other" | yes | Why: dropped (by the owner), split (the designer split it into new issues), triage (the triage agent dropped it), reconcile (reconcile found no live work behind the claim and took the issue out of the factory), rejected (released at its last allowed life and labelled factory:rejected), other. |
| `split_into` | array of integer | required | no |  | yes | split: the new issues it was split into; empty otherwise. |
| `why_split` | string | optional | yes |  |  | split: why the designer split the issue (size, areas touched, an owner decision or spike inside it, risk); null for any other abandon and for a split logged before the designer gave reasons. |
| `why_count` | string | optional | yes |  |  | split: why this many parts, not fewer or more; null otherwise. |
| `why_parts` | string | optional | yes |  |  | split: why the boundaries between the parts fall where they do; null otherwise. |
| `why_order` | string | optional | yes |  |  | split: why the blockedBy order is what it is, or that the parts are independent; null otherwise. |
| `child_whys` | array of string | optional | yes |  |  | split: what makes each new issue a part of its own, in the order of split_into; null otherwise. |
| `stage` | string | required | yes |  |  | reconcile and rejected: the stage callum-flow-factory-state showed the issue in, in its words, not a transition state; null otherwise. |
| `lives` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | reconcile and rejected: the released life's number among the issue's lives, when known; null otherwise. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The abandoned work's branch, when known. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The abandoned work's pull request, when there is one. |
| `detail` | string | required | yes |  |  | One line for people: the owner's note, or what reconcile checked. Never parse it. |

Example:

```json
{
  "reason": "dropped",
  "split_into": [],
  "why_split": null,
  "why_count": null,
  "why_parts": null,
  "why_order": null,
  "child_whys": null,
  "stage": null,
  "lives": null,
  "branch": null,
  "pr": null,
  "detail": "dropped"
}
```

## claim_lost

This device tried to claim the issue and another device holds it. Written by callum-flow-claim. Proof that two devices contended for one issue; this device does not work on it.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### claim_lost v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `holder` | string | required | yes |  |  | The device that holds the claim; null when it could not be read. |
| `holder_since` | string | required | yes |  |  | When the holder claimed it, as its claim comment says; null when not known. |
| `race` | boolean | required | no |  |  | true: both devices claimed at once and the other won; false: the issue was already held. |

Example:

```json
{
  "holder": "coder-dev-system-loop",
  "holder_since": "2026-10-16T09:12:40Z",
  "race": false
}
```

## claim_renewed

A heartbeat extended this device's claim on the issue. Written by callum-flow-claim --heartbeat. Housekeeping: not progress on the issue.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### claim_renewed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lease_minutes` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | How long the claim now holds from this event, in minutes. |

Example:

```json
{
  "lease_minutes": 120
}
```

## claimed

This device took the claim on the issue: no other device works on it while the lease holds. Written by callum-flow-claim. The claim ends with merged, closed, abandoned or requeued.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### claimed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lease_minutes` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | How long the claim holds without a renewal, in minutes. |
| `title` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 256 | yes | The issue's title as the producer read it, clipped to 256 characters; null when it was not read. An issue's newest title is the title of its newest ready or claimed event by ts that has a non-null title. |
| `labels` | array of string | optional | yes |  | yes | The issue's label names in GitHub's order, as the producer read them: on ready, the labels of the queue listing; on claimed, the labels after the claim (the ready label the claim removed is left out). Null when they were not read. |
| `parent` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The parent issue's number when the parent is in the same repo. Null when there is no parent, when the parent is in another repo, or when it was not read. |
| `score` | integer | optional | yes |  |  | The claim rule's score for this issue when it was claimed; null or absent when the claim was not scored. |
| `factors` | array of object | optional | yes |  |  | Each factor that added to the score, with its points, in the rule's order. |

Example:

```json
{
  "lease_minutes": 120
}
```

## closed

GitHub shows the issue closed, outside the factory's own merge. Written by callum-flow-sweep (actor sweep), and by the factory loop when it closes a split's tracker once every sub-issue is closed (reason completed). Ends a claim like merged does, but throughput and lead time count merged only. Two devices may both log it: count one per issue and reason.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: issue and reason

### closed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | string | required | yes |  | yes | GitHub's close reason as GitHub gives it: completed, not_planned or duplicate; null when GitHub gives none. |

Example:

```json
{
  "reason": "completed"
}
```

## finding_handled

The fixer fixed or declined one review finding. Written by the loop from the fixer's answer (actor fixer), one per finding. Declined findings over all handled ones is the reviewer's false-positive rate.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### finding_handled v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The branch the fixer worked on. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The pull request, when there is one. |
| `head` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The head after the fix step, when known. |
| `finding` | string | required | no | minLength 1 |  | The finding's id in the review, for example r1-2 (round 1, finding 2). |
| `outcome` | enum | required | no | one of "fixed", "declined" | yes | fixed: the fixer changed the code for it; declined: the fixer judged it wrong or not worth a change. |
| `detail` | string | required | no |  |  | The fixer's one-line reason, for people; never parse it. |

Example:

```json
{
  "branch": "issue-92-tunnel-token",
  "pr": 143,
  "head": "0821e6a3c0f4b1d2e5a6978877665544332211ff",
  "finding": "r1-2",
  "outcome": "declined",
  "detail": "Info, not blocking: the secrets are hex, so quotes or backslashes cannot occur; no change made."
}
```

## gate_run

One run of the stop gate in a writer's slot finished: the repo's gate commands ran, or the gate never got a turn. Written by the loop from the companion's gate lines. Not a stage and not progress. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (issue, life, seq, started_at).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (issue, life, seq, started_at)

### gate_run v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `life` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | Which life of the issue the gate ran in. |
| `seq` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The record's sequence in this life whose writer step ran the gate. |
| `head` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The slot's HEAD commit when the gate ran; null when it could not be read. |
| `result` | enum | required | no | one of "pass", "fail", "unknown" | yes | pass, fail (a command exited non-zero), or unknown (the gate could not run: its budget ran out, a command did not start, or it never got a turn within the wait cap). |
| `wait_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How long the gate waited for a turn, in milliseconds; 0 when it took a turn at once or there is no limit. |
| `run_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How long the gate ran once it held a turn, in milliseconds; 0 when it never ran. |
| `concurrency` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | How many gates could run at once when this one asked for a turn; null when there was no limit. |
| `queued_behind` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many gates held a turn or waited ahead of this one when it asked; 0 when it took a turn at once. |
| `started_at` | string | required | no | format date-time | yes | When the gate asked for its turn (before any wait). |

Example:

```json
{
  "life": "tn0brb",
  "seq": 6,
  "head": "0821e6a3c0f4b1d2e5a6978877665544332211ff",
  "result": "pass",
  "wait_ms": 184000,
  "run_ms": 412000,
  "concurrency": 1,
  "queued_behind": 2,
  "started_at": "2026-10-16T15:49:06.252Z"
}
```

## implementer_routed

The model for the issue's build step was chosen. Written by callum-flow-implementer-route before each build. Issues routed by hash are the fair sample for comparing the models.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### implementer_routed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The model alias chosen, for example sonnet or opus. |
| `reason` | enum | required | no | one of "label", "default", "hash", "fallback" | yes | label: a model:<alias> label on the issue; default: no Opus share is set; hash: the issue's bucket against the Opus share; fallback: the labels could not be read. |
| `bucket` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0; maximum 99 | yes | hash: the issue's stable bucket, 0 to 99 (Opus when below opus_pct); null otherwise. |
| `opus_pct` | integer | required | no | minimum 0; maximum 100 | yes | The configured share of issues routed to Opus, in percent. |

Example:

```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",
  "reason": "default",
  "bucket": null,
  "opus_pct": 0
}
```

## intervention

Someone had to step in where the plan did not foresee it: a person (an owner op, a push, a hand merge, a rescue), the loop's judge (the main conversation, running a control op through the control tool) or the loop with unplanned judgement or recovery (a triage, an unknown step, a park, a guard refusal). Written by the loop, and by hand for a rescue the loop cannot see. Not a stage and not progress. The issue is null for a fleet-level one (a restart, a settings edit). Count one per (issue, cause, fact); each row with a null fact counts.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): optional
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (issue, cause, fact)

### intervention v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `who` | enum | required | no | one of "person", "loop", "judge" | yes | person: a person did something; loop: the loop had to judge or recover; judge: the loop's judge (the main conversation) ran a control op through the control tool. |
| `cause` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z0-9-]+)?$` | yes | What happened, as a code of v2 SPEC 7.2: for example op:resume, push, hand-merge, rescue, restart, config-file, triage, park, unknown:timeout, free:load, fix:ci or guard:write. An open list: handle a code you do not know. |
| `life` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | The issue's life it happened in, as in transition; null when none applies. |
| `fact` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The key of the fact it records, so it is logged and counted once; null for a hand-recorded rescue. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The pull request involved, when there is one. |
| `detail` | string | required | no |  |  | One line for people saying what happened; empty when none was given. Never parse it. |

Example:

```json
{
  "who": "person",
  "cause": "op:drop",
  "life": null,
  "fact": "op:drop/i91/mvb4ci14",
  "pr": null,
  "detail": "drop 91"
}
```

## loop_entry

Loop bookkeeping that most consumers can ignore: one piece of the loop's own work (an agent step, a tell to the owner, or a task) changed status. Written by the loop's ledger. Never a stage or progress; it shows the device is at work, and the loop rebuilds its ledger's tells and tasks from it after a lost store.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): optional
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### loop_entry v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | required | no | one of "agent-step", "tell", "task" | yes | agent-step: an agent ran one step of an issue; tell: a message to the owner; task: a wake of the loop's model outside a planned step. |
| `key` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The ledger key: the work's identity across retries, for example i92/ltn0brb/review/0821e6a/r2/a1. |
| `status` | enum | required | no | one of "running", "done", "failed", "timed-out", "lost" | yes | The status it changed to. |
| `attempts` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Attempts of this key so far. |
| `class` | enum | required | no | one of "free", "owner", "drive", "develop", "start" | yes | The planner's class for the work. |
| `rule` | string | required | no | minLength 1 |  | The planner rule that planned it, for example S2 or S3. |
| `started_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When this attempt started. |
| `ended_at` | string | required | yes | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When it ended; null while running. |
| `agent_id` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The agent's id, for an agent step; null otherwise. |
| `wake` | string | required | yes |  |  | The wake's name, for a tell or task, for example parked; null otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "kind": "agent-step",
  "key": "i92/ltn0brb/review/0821e6a/r2/a1",
  "status": "done",
  "attempts": 1,
  "class": "drive",
  "rule": "S2",
  "started_at": "2026-10-16T15:59:42.324Z",
  "ended_at": "2026-10-16T16:00:11.254Z",
  "agent_id": "a20142b8cd21d3b2b",
  "wake": null
}
```

## loop_passes

Loop bookkeeping that most consumers can ignore: a summary of one UTC minute of the loop's passes (how many ended, how long they took, how many acted or threw), written once a minute while the loop runs. It shows the loop's pace and settings, never a stage or progress. Written by the loop's pass book.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### loop_passes v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | The start of the UTC minute summed up, inclusive. |
| `to_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | The end of that minute, exclusive: one minute after from_at. |
| `passes` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Passes that ended in the minute. 0 when none did; then every duration below is null. |
| `acting` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Of those passes, how many acted (did something rather than finding nothing to do). |
| `errors` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Of those passes, how many threw. |
| `mean_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean duration of the passes, in milliseconds, rounded; null when there was none. |
| `p50_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The median duration (nearest rank), in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `p90_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The 90th percentile duration (nearest rank), in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `max_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The longest duration, in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `acting_mean_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean duration of the acting passes, in milliseconds, rounded; null when none acted. |
| `idle_mean_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean duration of the passes that did not act, in milliseconds, rounded; null when every pass acted or there was none. |
| `mode` | enum | required | no | one of "off", "observe", "act" | yes | The loop's mode: off, observe (plans, does not act) or act. |
| `planner` | enum | required | no | one of "v1", "v2" | yes | Which planner the loop ran. |
| `pass_every_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The loop's configured time between passes, in milliseconds. |

Example:

```json
{
  "from_at": "2026-10-17T00:46:00.000Z",
  "to_at": "2026-10-17T00:47:00.000Z",
  "passes": 5,
  "acting": 5,
  "errors": 0,
  "mean_ms": 9457,
  "p50_ms": 6384,
  "p90_ms": 24804,
  "max_ms": 24804,
  "acting_mean_ms": 9457,
  "idle_mean_ms": null,
  "mode": "act",
  "planner": "v2",
  "pass_every_ms": 10000
}
```

## merged

A pull request for the issue was merged. Written by callum-flow-merge on the device that merged it, by the loop when it finds a merge that no merged event recorded, or by callum-flow-sweep (actor sweep) when it finds a merge on the issue's branch that no event recorded. Ends the claim; the end point of lead time and throughput. Count one per pr and head.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): optional
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: pr and head

### merged v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The merged pull request; null when the loop found a merge it cannot name. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The merged branch, when known. |
| `head` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The commit that was merged, when known. |
| `by` | enum | required | no | one of "factory", "hand" | yes | factory: the factory merged it; hand: a person merged it outside the factory. |
| `recovered` | boolean | required | no |  |  | true when the loop logged it afterwards because no merged event was recorded at the merge. |
| `files` | array of string | optional | yes | items: minLength 1 | yes | The repo-relative paths the merged pull request changed, taken from GitHub's pull request files at merge time. Complete up to GitHub's own cap on that list. null when unknown, for example on a recovered merge or a pr of null. |
| `additions` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The pull request's total lines added, as GitHub reports them at merge time. null when unknown. |
| `deletions` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The pull request's total lines deleted, as GitHub reports them at merge time. null when unknown. |

Example:

```json
{
  "pr": 141,
  "branch": "issue-85-usage-panel",
  "head": "f94eb46adde9adb19a154dc41e32877369596f3b",
  "by": "factory",
  "recovered": false
}
```

## ready

The issue was seen with the ready label: it is in the factory's queue. Written by queue-watch, which the loop runs each pass, once per issue newly seen. Starts the clock for lead time. Also carries the issue's title, labels and parent as the queue listing showed them.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### ready v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 256 | yes | The issue's title as the producer read it, clipped to 256 characters; null when it was not read. An issue's newest title is the title of its newest ready or claimed event by ts that has a non-null title. |
| `labels` | array of string | optional | yes |  | yes | The issue's label names in GitHub's order, as the producer read them: on ready, the labels of the queue listing; on claimed, the labels after the claim (the ready label the claim removed is left out). Null when they were not read. |
| `parent` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The parent issue's number when the parent is in the same repo. Null when there is no parent, when the parent is in another repo, or when it was not read. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

## requeued

The issue's claim was given back and the issue is in the queue again (ready label on), for any device to take. Written by callum-flow-sweep when a lease ran out, and by the loop's reconcile or factory-reconcile when it released a claim with no live work behind it and put the issue back in the queue. Ends the claim. A reconcile release that takes the issue out of the factory is abandoned instead.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### requeued v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | enum | required | no | one of "lease-expired", "reconcile" | yes | Why: lease-expired (no renewal in time) or reconcile (reconcile found no live work behind the claim and requeued it). |
| `stage` | string | required | yes |  |  | reconcile: the stage callum-flow-factory-state showed the issue in, in its words (queued, designing, implementing, in pipeline, parked), not a transition state; null otherwise. |
| `lives` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | reconcile: the released life's number among the issue's lives, when known; null otherwise. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The released work's branch, when known. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The released work's open pull request, when there is one. |
| `detail` | string | required | yes |  |  | reconcile: what was checked, one line for people; never parse it. null otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "reason": "lease-expired",
  "stage": null,
  "lives": null,
  "branch": null,
  "pr": null,
  "detail": null
}
```

## reviewed

One review of the issue's pull request finished. Written by the loop from the reviewer's answer. Not a stage and not progress. A retried write can repeat it: count one per answer_path.

- Counting key: answer_path

### reviewed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `pr` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The reviewed pull request. |
| `head` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The commit that was reviewed. |
| `verdict` | enum | required | no | one of "approve", "changes", "unknown" | yes | approve, changes (findings to fix), or unknown (no valid answer). |

  "errors": 1,
  "warnings": 0,
  "infos": 2,
  "reviewer": "adjudicator",

## shadow_read

One shadow compare made by a reader that has an old/new source switch: the command read the same keys from the old source and the new central one and counted where the answers differ. Written once per compare, not for an issue. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (repo, device, ts).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (repo, device, ts)

### shadow_read v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reader` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` | yes | Which reader was compared, an open family such as claim-events. |
| `tool` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The command that made the compare, such as callum-flow-sweep. |
| `compared` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many keys were compared. |
| `differences` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many keys whose answers differ, with both sides cut at the settle time. |
| `live_differences` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many keys whose answers differ on everything read, push lag included. |
| `diff_keys` | array of string | required | no | maxItems 50 |  | The keys that differ, at most 50. |
| `old_ok` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | Whether the central read of the old side succeeded. |
| `new_ok` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | Whether the central read of the new side succeeded. |
| `settle_seconds` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The settle time in seconds: both sides are cut this far back so push lag is not counted as a difference. |
| `detail` | string | required | yes | maxLength 500 |  | The first difference as old against new, or null when there is none. |
| `scope_floor` | string | optional | yes |  |  | The writing device's first time in the new store for the repo (ISO, whole seconds), or null when it has none. The compare leaves out of both sides the events of a device older than its floor, history the new store never held. |
| `out_of_scope` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 |  | How many events the floor left out of both sides, or null when the reader does not count them. |

Example:

```json
{
  "reader": "claim-events",
  "tool": "callum-flow-sweep",
  "compared": 42,
  "differences": 0,
  "live_differences": 0,
  "diff_keys": [],
  "old_ok": true,
  "new_ok": true,
  "settle_seconds": 120,
  "detail": null
}
```

### test_weakened v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The merged branch. |
| `pr` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The merged pull request. |
| `head` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The merged head. |
| `commit` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` |  | The flagged commit (short sha). |
| `restored` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when a later commit on the branch put the test back. |
| `kinds` | array of string | required | no | minItems 1 |  | What the commit did to the tests, one code each, for example removed-assertion. |

## transition

The loop's record of the issue changed: it moved to a new state, or its step, attempt or notes changed. Written by the loop on every record change, and again after a re-claim. It carries the whole record, so the loop rebuilds a lost record from the newest one; to_state is the issue's state for the factory tools. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (issue, life, seq).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (issue, life, seq)

### transition v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `life` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | Which life of the issue: one per pass through the factory, named by when its claim started (seconds, base 36). |
| `seq` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The record's sequence in this life: one more on every transition. |
| `table_row` | string | required | no | pattern `^([A-Z][0-9]+\|recovered)$` | yes | The row of the loop's transition table that fired, for example T9 or U1 (v2 SPEC 4.3); recovered when the loop rebuilt the record after losing the step's outcome, and then via is recovered too. |
| `from_state` | enum | required | yes | one of "queued", "designing", "building", "reviewing", "fixing", "merge-queue", "parked", "waiting", "closed", null | yes | The state before; null for a life's first transition. |
| `to_state` | enum | required | no | one of "queued", "designing", "building", "reviewing", "fixing", "merge-queue", "parked", "waiting", "closed" | yes | The state after: the issue's state from now on. |
| `via` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z0-9-]+)?$` | yes | A short code for what moved it, for example approve, fix:review, free:load, unknown:timeout, triage:retry, unreject, reclaim (logged again after a re-claim) or dual-write (logged again when the new log lacked it). An open list: handle a code you do not know. |
| `seq_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When this transition happened. Time transitions by this, not by the envelope ts: a transition logged again after a re-claim keeps its seq_at. |
| `state_since` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the issue entered to_state; earlier than seq_at when the state did not change. |
| `resume_to` | enum | required | yes | one of "queued", "designing", "building", "reviewing", "fixing", "merge-queue", "parked", "waiting", "closed", null | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: when to_state is queued, the state a new claim leads to; when parked, the state unparking leads to; when waiting, the state the loop resumes to once every condition in wait holds; null otherwise. |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The life's branch, fixed for the life. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The life's pull request; null until there is one. |
| `head` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The head commit a step last confirmed on origin; null before the first push. |
| `approved_patch` | string | required | yes |  |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: the patch id the reviewer approved; null until an approval. |
| `brief_url` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The URL of the design brief comment; null until the designer posts one. |
| `step` | enum | required | yes | one of "lease", "design", "build", "review", "fix", "queue", "triage", null | yes | The step this seq runs: the state's own step, or triage; null while waiting. |
| `attempt` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The attempt of that step, from 1. |
| `cut` | boolean | required | no |  |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: true when this attempt already had its one free re-run. |
| `triages` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: triage calls so far in this life. |
| `fixes` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: entries to fixing so far in this life. |
| `round` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Entries to reviewing so far in this life: the review round. |
| `question` | string | required | yes | maxLength 2000 | yes | parked: the question for the owner; null otherwise. For people; never parse it. |
| `wait` | array of object | optional | yes | minItems 1; maxItems 8 |  | waiting: the conditions the loop re-checks each pass; null otherwise |
| `why` | enum | required | yes | one of "merged", "merged-by-hand", "dropped", "split", "closed-on-github", "claim-lost", null | yes | closed: why the life ended; null otherwise. |
| `notes` | array of string | required | no | maxItems 8; items: maxLength 1000 | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: owner, triage and decline notes for this seq's step, oldest first. For people and the step's agent; never parse them. |
| `pr_closed_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: GitHub's closedAt of the newest hand-closed pull request the loop has handled, exactly as GitHub gave it (the loop compares it as text, so it is never reformatted); null when none. |
| `lives` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | This life's number among the issue's lives since the count last started; the issue is rejected at the configured maximum. |

Example:

```json
{
  "life": "tn0brb",
  "seq": 6,
  "table_row": "T11",
  "from_state": "fixing",
  "to_state": "reviewing",
  "via": "fix",
  "seq_at": "2026-10-16T15:59:06.252Z",
  "state_since": "2026-10-16T15:59:06.252Z",
  "resume_to": null,
  "branch": "issue-92-tunnel-token",
  "pr": 143,
  "head": "0821e6a3c0f4b1d2e5a6978877665544332211ff",
  "approved_patch": null,
  "brief_url": "https://github.com/cbundy/plant-console/issues/92#issuecomment-6219193862",
  "step": "review",
  "attempt": 1,
  "cut": false,
  "triages": 0,
  "fixes": 1,
  "round": 2,
  "question": null,
  "why": null,
  "notes": [],
  "pr_closed_at": null,
  "lives": 1
}
```

## untrusted_stripped

A read of GitHub content dropped text by untrusted authors, or refused an untrusted issue, pull request or comment outright. Written by callum-flow-issue-read. A security trail: the dropped text itself is never logged.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### untrusted_stripped v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | enum | required | no | one of "issue", "pr", "comment", "comments", "timeline", "list" |  | What was being read: an issue, a pull request or a comment (refused whole), or an issue's comments, its timeline or an issue list (items dropped). |
| `refused` | boolean | required | no |  |  | true: the whole item was refused because its author is untrusted; false: untrusted items were dropped from it. |
| `count` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 |  | How many items were dropped; null when refused. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The pull request read, when it was one. |

Example:

```json
{
  "source": "timeline",
  "refused": false,
  "count": 2,
  "pr": null
}
```

## usage

A reading of the Claude subscription's usage windows. Written by usage-check, which the loop runs on its schedule. Shows how close the device is to a rate limit.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### usage v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `available` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when a reading was had; false when no source gave one (then every reading field is null). |
| `five_hour_pct` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | Percent of the five-hour window used, rounded up. |
| `five_hour_resets_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time | yes | When the five-hour window resets. |
| `seven_day_pct` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | Percent of the most used seven-day window, rounded up. |
| `seven_day_resets_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time | yes | When that seven-day window resets. |
| `source` | enum | required | yes | one of "oauth", "statusline", null |  | Where the reading came from; null when unavailable. |
| `reasons` | array of string | required | no |  |  | When unavailable: why, one code per source tried, for example statusline:bad-snapshot; empty otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "available": true,
  "five_hour_pct": 21,
  "five_hour_resets_at": "2026-10-16T16:00:00.000Z",
  "seven_day_pct": 4,
  "seven_day_resets_at": "2026-10-23T11:00:00.000Z",
  "source": "oauth",
  "reasons": []
}
```

## wind_down

One stop of a workspace's loop finished winding down: the loop stopped taking new work, waited for the steps that were running (up to a cap), then stopped. Written once per stop, not for an issue. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (repo, device, requested_at).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (repo, device, requested_at)

### wind_down v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requested_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the stop was asked for. With outcome off it equals stopped_at. |
| `stopped_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the loop stopped. With outcome off it equals requested_at. |
| `waited_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How long the stop waited for running steps, in milliseconds; 0 with outcome off. |
| `cap_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The longest the stop was allowed to wait, in milliseconds. |
| `outcome` | enum | required | no | one of "idle", "cap", "now", "off" | yes | How the wait ended: idle (no step was left running), cap (the wait cap ran out and the rest were cut), now (stopped at once, running steps cut), or off (wind-down is off: no wait). |
| `running_at_request` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many steps were running when the stop was asked for. |
| `running_at_request_keys` | array of string | required | no |  |  | The loop keys of those steps (stepKey i<N>/l<life>/s<seq>/<step>/a<n>, or reviewKey i<N>/l<life>/review/<patch7>/r<round>/a<n>). |
| `cut_at_stop` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many steps were still running, and cut, when the loop stopped. |
| `cut_at_stop_keys` | array of string | required | no |  | yes | The loop keys of the cut steps, in the same form as running_at_request_keys. Lifted as a jsonb column so a cut step can be joined to its re-run. |
| `trigger` | string | required | yes | one of "restart-self", "coder-stop", null | yes | What asked for the stop: restart-self, coder-stop, or null when not known. |

Example:

```json
{
  "requested_at": "2026-10-17T10:00:00.000Z",
  "stopped_at": "2026-10-17T10:04:10.500Z",
  "waited_ms": 250500,
  "cap_ms": 300000,
  "outcome": "idle",
  "running_at_request": 2,
  "running_at_request_keys": [
    "i840/ltn0brb/s6/build/a1",
    "i841/ltn0brc/review/0821e6a/r2/a1"
  ],
  "cut_at_stop": 0,
  "cut_at_stop_keys": [],
  "trigger": "restart-self"
}
```
